title: Re Attached Report By The Shanghai Times On The John Thorburn Case

page_data.en:
Form No. 2.
G. 21,860-T-31

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
（印：REPORT）

File No.
& Section
S. D. 2447
Date July 23, 1931
23-7-31

Subject (in full) Re attached report by the Shanghai Times on the John Thorburn case.

Made by. D. S. Golder. Forwarded by D.B.Km A1.

In the July 23rd issue of the above newspaper, a report appears which sets forth in detail the arrest of John Thorburn as witnessed by a Catholic priest residing at Henli.
Mr. W. J. Mills of the H.B.M. Consulate was interviewed regarding the veracity of the report, he stated that no such report had been made to the Consulate, but that the British Authorities were investigating the matter. Mr. Mills expressed doubt as to the report in view of the fact that 7 weeks have elapsed since the reported occurence took place.

D. S. Golder
Officer i/c Special Branch.

S2, Further report later please.
JMc.
24:7:31.

S2, Please prepare a summary in the form of a diary of the action taken by the Municipal Police in connection with the efforts to find Thorburn. The diary should in addition give an outline of the history of the case, and important happenings connected with it known to the Police.
JMc. 29/7

上海公共租界工部局警务处
（印：报告）

档案编号
及部门
S. D. 2447
日期 1931年7月23日
23-7-31

事由（全称） 关于《字林西报》就约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）一案所附报道的事宜。

呈报人：D. S. Golder。转呈人：D.B.Km A1。

在上述报纸7月23日的刊期中，刊登了一篇报道，详细陈述了居住在恒利（Henli，音译）的一位天主教神父所目击的约翰·索恩伯恩被捕经过。
就此报道的真实性采访了英国驻沪领事馆的W. J. Mills先生，他表示领事馆未收到此类报告，但英国当局正在调查此事。鉴于据报道事件发生至今已过去7周，Mills先生对该报道表示怀疑。

D. S. Golder
特别处处长。

S2，请随后提交进一步报告。
JMc.
1931年7月24日。

S2，请以日记形式编制一份摘要，记录工部局警务处为寻找索恩伯恩所采取的行动。该日记还应概述该案的历史沿革，以及警方所知的与之相关的重要事件。
JMc. 7月29日

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 28, 1931

Additional Evidence Is
Found Thorburn Was
Arrested By Gendarmerie

PRIEST TELLS OF VISIT FROM BRITISH
YOUTH DURING NIGHT OF JUNE 1 AND
SUBSEQUENT ARREST BY SOLDIERS

STRUGGLES WITH CAPTORS AND RECEIVES
BAYONET WOUND IN NECK

Appeal Of Local British Residents Received In
London; Reply From Back Stating Action
Will Be Taken; Chinese Comment

“The Shanghai Times” is able to give additional
indisputable evidence of the fate of John Thorburn, 18-
year-old British resident of Shanghai, who has been missing
for over seven weeks, was actually arrested in the vicinity
of Quinsan by Chinese military police. The evidence has
been furnished by a Catholic priest who actually sheltered
Thorburn on the night of June 1 and, later, saw him seized
by Chinese police and taken off to Quinsan. The evidence
also shows that Thorburn broke away from his captors and
dashed down the railway line where he was intercepted and
again arrested after a struggle, during which he was wound-
ed in the neck by a bayonet carried by one of the soldiers.
What happened to Thorburn after his second arrest is a
mystery which the entire foreign community of Shanghai is
anxious to solve, with or without the aid of the Chinese
authorities.

This further proof of Thor-
burn’s arrest has come from a
reliable source. The report gives
details of the arrest as actually
witnessed by our informant, a
Catholic priest, who has since
been unable to ascertain what
happened to Thorburn after he
was taken away by the Chinese
police in the direction of the
Quinsan railway station.

It will be recalled that Thor-
burn left Shanghai presumably
by train for Quinsan and Suzhou
on the morning of June 1. He
was seen at Hongkew later in
Quinsan at about 4 p.m. On the
night of June 1 Thorburn appear-
ed at the abode of the Catholic
priest near the railway station and
asked for food and shelter, and
after a time, he called at the house of a number of residents in the neighbourhood, Mr. Sussman
and Heath. The priest knew
Thorburn well by sight and had
conversed with him on numerous
occasions. On the night of June
1, shortly after 10 o’clock, Thor-
burn knocked at the door of the
priest’s home and was admitted.
He was in a bedraggled condition
and was wet through. He ex-
plained his condition by mention-
ing something about falling into a
canal. His questions were asked
and Thorburn’s clothes were re-
moved and dried. He was pro-
vided with dry garments while
this was being done.

Next morning Thorburn took
his leave of the priest and was
only a few yards away when
some Chinese soldiers seized him
and shouted in Chinese “There’s
that Kweitsze”. They immediately
seized him and led him off in the
direction of Quinsan. He was
locked up temporarily in a small
house, but somehow managed to
break out, and fled once again in
the direction of the priest’s house.
Pursued by soldiers, Thor-
burn ran along the railway
line. He was finally overtaken
and captured. Thorburn struggled
violently but was finally over-
come, receiving a bayonet wound
in the neck during the struggle.
Just how serious the wound was
the priest was unable to say, as
Thorburn was hurried off in the
direction of the Quinsan railway
station. That was the last seen
of Thorburn by the priest.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1931年7月28日，星期四

发现额外证据表明
索恩伯恩曾被宪兵逮捕

神父讲述6月1日夜英国青年来访
及随后被士兵逮捕经过

与抓捕者搏斗并颈部受刺刀伤

在沪英国居民发出的抗议已获伦敦受理；
回电称将采取行动；中方评论

《字林西报》能够提供额外的确凿证据，证明在上海居住、已失踪七个多周的18岁英国居民约翰·索恩伯恩的命运，他实际上是在昆山附近被中国军警逮捕的。该证据由一位天主教神父提供，他在6月1日晚确实庇护了索恩伯恩，后来亲眼目睹他被中国警察抓获并带往昆山。证据还显示，索恩伯恩从抓捕者手中逃脱，沿铁路线奔跑，但在拦截后再次被捕，期间经过一番搏斗，被一名士兵用刺刀刺伤颈部。索恩伯恩第二次被捕后遭遇如何，是一个谜团，整个上海外侨社群都急于解开这个谜团，无论是否有中国当局的协助。

这一关于索恩伯恩被捕的进一步证据来自可靠来源。该报告详细描述了逮捕过程，均由我们的线人——一位天主教神父——亲眼目睹，但他此后一直无法查明索恩伯恩被中国警察带往昆山火车站方向后发生了什么事。

回顾此前情况，索恩伯恩于6月1日上午 presumably（据信）乘火车离开上海前往昆山和苏州。当天下午4点左右，有人在虹口，随后在昆山见到过他。6月1日晚，索恩伯恩出现在火车站附近那位天主教神父的住所，请求食物和住宿，过了一会儿，他又拜访了附近几位居民的住宅，包括Sussman先生和Heath先生。这位神父对索恩伯恩的面容很熟悉，并曾多次与他交谈。6月1日晚10点刚过，索恩伯恩敲响了神父家的门并被允许进入。他浑身湿透，衣衫褴褛。他解释说自己的状况是因为掉进了运河。有人询问了他的情况，他的衣服被脱下烘干。在此期间，为他提供了干燥的衣物。

第二天早上，索恩伯恩向神父告辞，刚走出几码远，就被几名中国士兵抓住，并用中文喊道：“就是那个鬼子”。他们立即抓住他，将他带往昆山方向。他被暂时关押在一间小屋里，但不知何故设法逃了出来，再次朝神父家的方向逃跑。
在士兵的追捕下，索恩伯恩沿着铁路线奔跑。他最终被追上并抓获。索恩伯恩激烈反抗，但最终被制服，在搏斗中颈部被刺刀刺伤。神父无法说明伤势有多严重，因为索恩伯恩被匆忙带往昆山火车站方向。那是神父最后一次见到索恩伯恩。

1894

Other Testimony
Other witnesses examined by
Mr. A. L. Scott, British Vice-
Consul, have stated that Thorburn
had his arms tied behind his back
and was taken by train from
Quinsan to Soochow. Witnesses
also stated that Thorburn was
seen in Soochow, wounded and,
an unconfirmed report states,
mutilated.
In the light of this fresh
evidence it appears beyond ques-
tion that Thorburn was arrested
by the Chinese military at Quin-
san and was actually taken to the
Quinsan railway station where he
was entrained for Soochow.

Another Protest
In the meantime indignation in
Shanghai is growing daily. The
cabled protest signed by over
2,300 British residents has reach-
ed London where Mr. F. H. Cross-
ley, formerly of Shanghai, who
has cabled receipt of the protest,
will see that it reaches the right
quarters.
Still another national society
has interested itself in the dis-
appearance of Thorburn. Yester-
day the Shanghai branch of the
Anzac Society, consisting of local
Australians and New Zealanders,
forwarded the following tele-
graphic protest to the British
Prime Minister:
Shanghai Anzac Society consist-
ing of Anzacs who fought in Great
War and Australians New Zea-
landers resident China record
strongest indignation disappearance
John Thorburn (stop) Despite con-
clusive evidence of arrest obtained
by British Authorities Chinese
Government deny all knowledge of

1894

其他证词
英国副领事A. L. Scott先生讯问的其他证人表示，索恩伯恩的双臂被绑在背后，并由火车从昆山带往苏州。证人还表示，有人在苏州看到过受伤的索恩伯恩，还有一份未经证实的报告称其身体受到残害。
鉴于这些新证据，索恩伯恩在昆山被中国军队逮捕，并确实被带往昆山火车站，随后乘车前往苏州，这似乎已毫无疑问。

另一项抗议
与此同时，上海的愤怒情绪日益高涨。由2300多名英国居民签署的电报抗议书已抵达伦敦，前居上海的F. H. Crossley先生已发电报确认收到该抗议书，并将确保其送达相关部门。
又有一个全国性团体关注起索恩伯恩的失踪案。昨天，由在沪澳大利亚人和新西兰人组成的澳新军团协会（Anzac Society）上海分会，向英国首相发出了以下电报抗议：
上海澳新军团协会，成员包括参加大战的澳新军团士兵以及居住在中国的澳大利亚人和新西兰人，记录对约翰·索恩伯恩失踪一事的强烈愤慨（停）尽管英国当局已获得确凿的逮捕证据，中国政府仍否认知情
